479:These proportions use the same test data that defines the headroom, introducing circularity: $\delta$ is anchored to the very quantity it contextualizes.

932:CoNLL alignment is moderate ($\rho{\approx}0.51$), but the valid-instance fraction is low (38\% for Qwen, 11\% for LLaMA) because degeneracy eliminates most headroom before alignment can operate.
933:LP-quality alignment is the primary predictor of selection direction; degeneracy constrains headroom but does not independently predict whether LP selection gains materialize (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
1015:\caption{Selection $\Delta$ (pp over single-sample) stratified by VC quartile on SciERC ($N{=}8$, Qwen3-8B). Oracle headroom collapses at Q4; LP rankings are unreliable at Q1--Q2. Neither quartile supports consistent selection gains.}
1036:\item \textbf{Q4 ceiling effect.} High-consistency instances (mean VC${=}0.92$) have oracle headroom of only 4.78~pp. Samples have already converged, leaving little room for any signal to improve selection.
1037:\item \textbf{Q1--Q2 noise.} Low-consistency instances retain large headroom (14--17~pp) but LP rankings are unreliable, and LP rankings produce inconsistent $\Delta$ signs across quartiles.
1054:Oracle headroom is $+18.1$\,pp (greedy $0.404$, oracle $0.585$), the largest of any configuration, confirming that correct answers exist among samples but no signal recovers them.
1062:Table~\ref{tab:re_cond_selection} presents RE selection at $N{=}8$: no signal outperforms single-sample (0.404) on the full set ($n{=}397$) or the non-zero subset ($n{=}238$), with 18.1~pp of unrealized oracle headroom.
1067:Selection remains below single-sample on RE ($\Delta$ up to $-3.4$~pp) despite 17.1~pp of oracle headroom.
1078:Oracle headroom exists (0.757 vs.\ 0.674) but no signal exploits it, ruling out the 40\% zero-F1 floor effect as the explanation for RE selection failure.
1106:Even the most favorable seed captures only ${\sim}9\%$ of the 17.1~pp oracle headroom.
1266:Few-NERD and SciERC ($\beta_{\textup{crit,eff}} {<} 1$) show significantly negative $\Delta$, indicating that even where structural headroom exists, marginal-entity precision is insufficient.

1509:\paragraph{$N$-scaling: selection headroom vs.\ selection gain.}
1510:Table~\ref{tab:n_scaling_selection} traces the effect of sample count on degeneracy, oracle headroom, and per-signal selection gain.
1511:Oracle headroom grows roughly linearly with $N$ ($+4.4$~pp at $N{=}2$ to $+20.0$~pp at $N{=}32$).
1512:LP selection improves monotonically with $N$ ($+0.39$~pp at $N{=}8$ to $+0.95$~pp at $N{=}32$), but even at $N{=}32$, where degeneracy falls to 4\% and oracle headroom reaches ${\sim}20$~pp, the best signal captures less than 5\% of the available improvement.

1636:LP-weighted construction yields $+1.53$\,pp on SciERC 72B ZS ($p{=}0.008$, CI [$+0.25$, $+2.82$]), recovering $10.2$\% of headroom. Construction fails on Few-NERD ($-0.20$\,pp) and CoNLL ($-0.37$\,pp) where degeneracy exceeds $46$\%---consistent with FT-regime degeneracy gating.

2046:At finer per-type granularity, selection depends on the interaction of degeneracy, oracle headroom, and type-specific LP-quality alignment.

2119:LP selection does not yield significant gains at any training duration ($-1.24$, $+0.64$, $+1.02$~pp; all below the ${\approx}$1.5~pp MDE), despite oracle headroom ranging from 8.4 to 15.0~pp.
2406:Degeneracy ${>}30$\% indicates limited headroom for any selection or aggregation strategy.
2422:Report: (1)~degeneracy percentage, (2)~oracle headroom (oracle $-$ greedy), (3)~signal $\rho$ (cross-instance and within-instance), (4)~selection $\Delta$F1 with bootstrap $p$-values and effect sizes (Cohen's $d$), (5)~construction $\Delta$F1, (6)~selective prediction AUPRC and coverage--F1 curve.

\paragraph{Oracle ceiling scaling law.}
Oracle F1 follows $F_1(N) = a - b \cdot N^{-c}$, with $R^2 > 0.999$ across all model--dataset fits (Figure~\ref{fig:oracle_scaling}).
The exponent $c$ varies with dataset complexity: Few-NERD ($c{\approx}0.61$) scales comparably to reasoning-task estimates ($c{\approx}0.5$--$0.7$; \citealp{brown2024monkeys}), while SciERC converges more slowly ($c{\approx}0.35$), consistent with complex IE producing less marginal diversity per additional sample.
CoNLL's narrow headroom ($b{=}0.04$--$0.10$) makes $c$ unreliable (inter-model variance $2.5{\times}$); we report only $a$ and $b$ for CoNLL.
A single stochastic sample ($N{=}1$, $T{=}1.0$) underperforms greedy by 1--3\,pp because sampling noise outweighs diversity; $N{\geq}4$ is needed to match greedy.


\paragraph{Degeneracy and inverse scaling.}\label{app:degen_inverse}
Table~\ref{tab:degen_inverse} stratifies $N$-transitions by instance degeneracy status across all dataset--regime combinations.
Degenerate instances exhibit near-zero inverse scaling ($1.3$\% vs.\ $11.1$\% for non-degenerate; OR${=}0.109$, $p{<}10^{-300}$, Fisher's exact test over $195{,}675$ transitions).
This is expected: degenerate instances produce identical entity sets across all $N$ samples, so MV F1 is constant by construction---they cannot exhibit inverse scaling.
The effect holds across all settings (Table~\ref{tab:degen_inverse}), with the sole exception of SciERC pretrained ($p{=}0.083$), where low degeneracy (${\leq}10$\%) yields too few degenerate transitions for adequate power.
Pretrained models show a stronger protective effect (OR${=}0.066$ vs.\ $0.166$ for finetuned), consistent with higher overall inverse scaling rates creating more room for the degeneracy--stability association.

3	Sections~\ref{sec:selection_gap}--\ref{sec:theory} developed the diagnostic framework on SciERC; this section extends it across datasets and models.

5	\subsection{Experimental Setup}\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	\paragraph{Datasets.}
8	We evaluate on four English NER benchmarks spanning a difficulty gradient.
9	\textbf{SciERC} \cite{luan2018scierc} (551 test instances, 6 entity types) is the primary medium-difficulty test bed (${\approx}$65\% F1).
10	\textbf{Few-NERD} \cite{ding2021fewnerd} (INTRA coarse; 37{,}648 instances, 8 entity types, ${\approx}$75\% F1) provides a low-degeneracy contrast where LP selection succeeds (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}).
11	\textbf{CoNLL-2003} \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll} (3{,}453 test sentences, 4 entity types, ${\approx}$91\% F1) serves as a ceiling-effect control.
12	\textbf{WNUT-17} \cite{derczynski2017wnut} (1{,}287 social media instances, 53.7\% zero F1) probes the signal-collapse boundary.
13	
14	\paragraph{Models and sampling.}
15	\textbf{Qwen3-8B} and \textbf{LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct} are Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuned using LLaMA Factory \cite{zheng2024llamafactory} (Appendix~\ref{app:training}; Few-NERD uses 3 epochs vs.\ 5 for others; Appendix~\ref{app:epoch_confound}).
16	$N{=}8$ samples at $T{=}1.0$ (primary) with vLLM constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided}; $N {\in} \{16, 32, 64\}$ for scaling (Figure~\ref{fig:n_scaling}; Appendix~\ref{app:n_scaling}). Thinking-token impact on LP is negligible ($<$2.7\% of median range; Appendix~\ref{app:thinking_token}).
17

23	\end{figure}

26	\subsection{Quality Estimation Results}\label{sec:qe_results}
27	
28	Table~\ref{tab:multiseed} presents $\rho$ and AUROC for five signals on SciERC across NER and RE tasks with both model families (Appendix~\ref{app:multiseed}).
29	
30	\paragraph{Signal rankings are difficulty-dependent.}
31	On SciERC, structural signals lead (VC $\rho{=}0.379$, SJ $0.360$) over LP ($0.205$); bootstrap CIs confirm the gap ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.151{\pm}0.006$, 5 seeds; Appendix~\ref{app:bootstrap_signal}).
32	Under seed-replication Holm--Bonferroni correction ($k{=}5$ seeds), the SJ~${>}$~LP advantage reaches $p_{\text{adj}}{=}0.013$ (Appendix~\ref{app:bootstrap_signal}).
33	On CoNLL (F1${\approx}$0.91), EM leads both $\rho$ and AUROC ($0.816$).
34	At the signal-collapse boundary (WNUT-17, F1${\approx}$42\%), full-set correlations are dominated by the zero/non-zero boundary (VC $\rho{=}0.724$ at $N{=}16$, but conditional $\rho{=}0.038$; Table~\ref{tab:wnut}); LP shows the reverse (conditional $\rho{=}0.350$; Figure~\ref{fig:signal_heatmap}).

1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}\label{sec:selection_method}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	\paragraph{When test-time scaling fails for NER.}
4	For discrete-answer reasoning, sample diversity reflects diverse reasoning paths; for NER, degeneracy ($12$--$68$\%) reduces candidate diversity while signal alignment collapse ($\alpha{\to}0$) limits ranking.
5	The degeneracy decomposition (\S\ref{sec:theory}) identifies $\alpha$, not degeneracy, as the binding constraint ($8$--$33{\times}$ tighter); this persists across families \cite{yun2025price}, scales (4B--72B), and decoding modes (Appendix~\ref{app:freeform_ablation}).
6	The diagnostic framework that identifies these co-occurring conditions is our primary contribution (Appendices~\ref{app:objections},~\ref{app:cost_benefit}).
7	At $N{=}8$, high degeneracy ($>50$\%) suggests scaling will not help; low degeneracy with strong LP-F1 alignment may warrant entity construction; otherwise, greedy remains the default (Appendices~\ref{app:recommendations},~\ref{app:when_selection_works}).

\midrule

The full-set $p$-values are: VC ${<}$1e-112, FK $p{=}0.001$, SJ $p{=}0.020$, EM $p{=}0.194$, LP ${<}$1e-28.
VC's high full-set $\rho{=}0.724$ is entirely attributable to the zero/non-zero boundary (conditional $\rho{=}0.038$, $p{=}0.49$), while LP's conditional $\rho{=}0.350$ is the highest among all signals on the non-zero subset, full-set correlations on high-failure-rate datasets conflate binary success prediction with quality gradation.

\paragraph{Cross-configuration selection analysis.}
Table~\ref{tab:cross_selection} extends the selection analysis to five additional configurations.
On LLaMA SciERC, where output diversity remains substantial (18\% identical outputs, 39\% unique), LP achieves the highest selection F1 (0.652) at $N{=}8$ but still falls within bootstrap noise of single-sample (0.646), replicating the gap observed on Qwen SciERC (Table~\ref{tab:selection}).
On LLaMA Few-NERD ($n{=}32{,}565$, 3-seed mean), LP is the only signal with positive selection ($+0.36$~pp), consistent with LP being the most stable positive signal across model families (Qwen Few-NERD: $+1.39$~pp, Table~\ref{tab:fewnerd}). All structural signals degrade selection (VC $-2.39$~pp, SJ $-0.52$~pp), consistent with the Qwen pattern. LLaMA Few-NERD degeneracy ($23.4{\pm}4.7$\%, 3 seeds) is higher than Qwen ($13.0$\%), illustrating the capability-diversity tension: LLaMA achieves stronger greedy F1 ($0.784$ vs.\ $0.748$, $+3.6$~pp) but at the cost of higher degeneracy ($+10.4$~pp) and reduced oracle headroom ($10.0$ vs.\ $12.4$~pp).
On CoNLL, 48--87\% of instances produce identical outputs across all $N$ samples; this reflects a ceiling effect (single-sample F1 ${\approx}$0.91--0.92) rather than signal failure, and selection analysis on these configurations is uninformative because there is little per-sample variance for any signal to exploit.

\paragraph{Capability stratification.}
SJ effectiveness scales with structural complexity: on SciERC instances with 6+ entities, $\rho{=}0.547$, compared to $\rho{=}0.415$ for 1--2 entities.
Similarly, RE instances with ${\geq}3$ relation triples ($n{=}81$) yield substantially stronger correlations (Voting $\rho{=}0.630$, SJ $\rho{=}0.502$), demonstrating that within the model's capability range, increased output complexity amplifies structural signal advantage.
The SJ advantage over logprob remains stable across sentence-length quartiles ($\Delta\rho{\approx}0.08$--$0.20$), and three independent complexity proxies (entity count, sentence length, relation density) show weak mutual correlation ($|r|{<}0.15$), indicating a genuinely multi-dimensional benefit rather than a single confound.

\paragraph{Method boundary: WNUT-17.}
WNUT-17 establishes where the approach breaks down.
SJ achieves $\rho{=}0.062$ ($p{=}0.106$, not statistically significant), with 54\% of instances at zero F1.
Log-probability shows a strong \textit{negative} correlation ($\rho{=}{-}0.411$): the model is confidently wrong on novel entities, a calibration failure that no post-hoc consistency signal can remedy.
This is a boundary of the method, not a limitation of the datasets.

\small
\caption{Signal robustness across temperature and sample size on SciERC (Spearman $\rho$). $^\dagger$Mean over 3 seeds ($\sigma{=}0.025$; individual: 0.428, 0.424, 0.384). RE results are preliminary (single dataset).}

151	\paragraph{Quality estimation $\neq$ output selection.}
152	We attribute this gap (Figure~\ref{fig:selection_gap}) to a fundamental distinction: instance-level confidence signals predict \textit{which inputs} the model handles reliably, not \textit{which output} among $N$ candidates is best for a given input.
153	When per-sample variance is low relative to instance-level difficulty---as in NER, where the model often produces $N$ similar extractions---even perfect quality estimation cannot discriminate among near-identical candidates.
154	
155	\paragraph{Implications for test-time scaling.}
156	This correlation-selection gap has direct consequences for test-time scaling in IE \cite{brown2024monkeys, snell2024scaling}.
157	Scaling inference compute through repeated sampling assumes a selector can identify the best sample.
158	Our results show that for structured prediction, existing confidence signals serve as quality \textit{estimators}---useful for flagging unreliable predictions---but not as effective \textit{selectors}.
159	Closing this gap likely requires signals that capture per-sample rather than per-instance variation, such as trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers} or pairwise comparison models.

162	\subsection{Task Complexity and Signal Robustness}
163	\label{sec:complexity_robustness}
164	
165	\paragraph{Task difficulty as a boundary condition.}
166	Signal effectiveness varies systematically with task difficulty.
167	On CoNLL (greedy micro F1${>}$0.91), EM leads all signals ($\rho{=}0.451$); on SciERC NER (micro F1$\,{\approx}\,$0.66), SJ overtakes EM ($\rho{=}0.357$ vs.\ 0.257); on SciERC RE, where 44\% of instances score zero F1, all signals converge to $\rho{\approx}0.25$.
168	The NER--RE difference is statistically confirmed: Fisher's $z$-test comparing SJ $\rho$ between NER ($\rho{=}0.357$) and RE ($\rho{=}0.211$) yields $z{=}2.31$, $p{=}0.021$, confirming statistically significant task-dependent degradation.
169	
170	\paragraph{Per-relation diagnostic.}
171	RE signal degradation is relation-specific.
172	\textsc{Feature-Of} has near-zero correlation ($\rho{=}0.004$), while \textsc{Hyponym-Of} achieves $\rho{=}0.646$.
173	The primary bottleneck is entity span errors, which account for 55.5\% of RE false negatives---a prerequisite failure that consistency signals cannot detect, as they measure agreement among equally incorrect extractions.
174	
175	\paragraph{Capability stratification.}
176	SJ effectiveness scales with structural complexity: on SciERC instances with 6+ entities, $\rho{=}0.547$, compared to $\rho{=}0.415$ for 1--2 entities.
177	Similarly, RE instances with ${\geq}3$ relation triples ($n{=}81$) yield substantially stronger correlations (Voting $\rho{=}0.630$, SJ $\rho{=}0.502$), demonstrating that within the model's capability range, increased output complexity amplifies structural signal advantage.
178	The SJ advantage over logprob remains stable across sentence-length quartiles ($\Delta\rho{\approx}0.08$--$0.20$), and three independent complexity proxies (entity count, sentence length, relation density) show weak mutual correlation ($|r|{<}0.15$), indicating a genuinely multi-dimensional benefit rather than a single confound.
179	
180	\paragraph{Method boundary: WNUT-17.}
181	WNUT-17 establishes where the approach breaks down.
182	SJ achieves $\rho{=}0.062$ ($p{=}0.106$, not statistically significant), with 54\% of instances at zero F1.
183	Log-probability shows a strong \textit{negative} correlation ($\rho{=}{-}0.411$): the model is confidently wrong on novel entities, a calibration failure that no post-hoc consistency signal can remedy.
184	This is a boundary of the method, not a limitation of the datasets.

Our evaluation covers three datasets but only one RE benchmark (SciERC), where 44\% of instances receive zero F1, compressing the discriminable range and limiting signal differentiation for relation extraction.
WNUT-17 confirms the capability boundary of our approach, but our positive results on formal-domain text (CoNLL, SciERC) have not been validated on informal or noisy text where models achieve non-trivial performance.

We evaluate two model families (Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B), both at 8B parameters.
Whether our findings---particularly the correlation-selection gap and the structural-over-surface signal ordering---hold for larger models (70B+) or closed-source APIs remains untested.
Larger models may produce higher-quality and more diverse samples, potentially altering the signal landscape.

Our analysis of selection potential uses unsupervised signals.
We do not train a dedicated verifier or reward model, leaving unknown how much of the oracle headroom a supervised approach could recover.

We evaluate at $N{=}8$ and $N{=}16$.
The behavior of confidence signals at larger sample sizes (e.g., $N{=}64$ or $N{=}128$) is unknown, and $N$-scaling gains are setting-dependent: SJ improves by $+0.071$ on Qwen SciERC NER but only $+0.016$ on LLaMA SciERC NER when doubling from $N{=}8$ to $N{=}16$.

On CoNLL, the SJ--FK gap is only 0.004 ($\rho{=}0.436$ vs.\ $0.431$ for LLaMA), so the structural advantage over surface signals may not generalize to all simple-schema datasets.
Finally, log-probability was excluded from the temperature comparison ($T{=}0.7$ vs.\ $T{=}1.0$) due to missing $T{=}0.7$ logprob data, leaving its temperature sensitivity uncharacterized.

1	# WNUT-17 数据质量诊断报告 (exp_003)
2	
3	## 概要
4	
5	**根因：训练数据空实例比例过高（63.8%），导致模型过度倾向于预测"无实体"。**
6	
7	这不是数据转换 bug，而是训练数据构造策略问题叠加 WNUT-17 固有难度。
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 方向 1：数据格式转换检查
12	
13	### 转换脚本 (convert_wnut17.py)
14	- BIO→span 转换逻辑正确，与标准 BIO 解码一致
15	- Entity type mapping 正确：6 types (corporation, creative-work, group, location, person, product)
16	- Char offset 计算正确（基于 space-joined tokens）
17	- 脚本内含 validation：检查 text[start:end] == entity_text
18	
19	### 数据格式
20	- test.json: JSONL 格式，1287 行，`load_uie_jsonl()` 正常加载
21	- train.json: JSONL 格式，3394 行
22	
23	### Prompt 模板差异（次要问题）
24	训练与推理 prompt 有轻微不一致：
25	- **训练**: `Output format: {"entities": [...], "relations": [...], "events": []}` + `For relations, head is the subject entity...`
26	- **推理**: `Output format: {"entities": [{"text": "...", "type": "...", "start": <int>, "end": <int>}], ...}`（无 relations 说明行）
27	
28	影响有限，因为模型理解核心指令，且 XGrammar 约束解码保证输出格式。
29	
30	**结论：数据转换本身无 bug。**
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 方向 2：Greedy 输出抽查
35	
36	### F1=0 实例分类（共 355 个，金标非空）
37	
38	| 类别 | 数量 | 占比 | 说明 |
39	|------|------|------|------|
40	| 模型输出为空 | 260 | 73.2% | **主要失败模式** |
41	| Span 边界不匹配 | 49 | 13.8% | 模型预测了实体但位置偏移 |
42	| Type 不匹配 | 46 | 13.0% | 位置正确但类型错误 |
43	
44	### 典型案例
45	
46	**模型输出空（260 例）：**
47	- `"( Source : ANI )"` → gold: ANI (group), pred: 空
48	- `"Watch What Else is Making News"` → gold: What Else is Making News (creative-work), pred: 空
49	- `"Wow , / r / news totally kicked..."` → gold: /r/news (group), /r/politics (group), pred: 空
50	- `"they changed all the topics to Zlatan"` → gold: Zlatan (product), pred: 空
51	- `"Bhangra is Punjabi"` → gold: Bhangra (person), Punjabi (location), pred: 空
52	
53	**Span 边界错误（49 例）：**
54	- gold `Gurez sector` (33-45) → pred `Gurez` (33-38)：漏标 "sector"
55	- gold `Rajesh Kalia` (164-176) → pred `Colonel Rajesh Kalia` (156-176)：多标 title
56	- gold `Chad` (6-10) → pred `Rip Chad` (2-10)
57	
58	**Type 错误（46 例）：**
59	- gold `Zlatan` = product → pred `Zlatan` = person（合理歧义）
60	- 部分 WNUT-17 金标本身有争议（如 `Bhangra` 标为 person 而非 creative-work）
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 方向 3：Gold Empty 实例处理
65	
66	### 数据分布
67	
68	| | 训练集 | 测试集 |
69	|---|---|---|
70	| 总实例数 | 3394 | 1287 |
71	| 空实体实例 | 2166 (63.8%) | 598 (46.5%) |
72	| 有实体实例 | 1228 (36.2%) | 689 (53.5%) |
73	
74	### 评估处理
75	
76	report.json 中 `n_gold_empty_filtered: 598` 表明评估代码**正确过滤**了 gold empty 实例：
77	- "full" 集 n=689（排除 gold empty）
78	- "conditional" 集 n=334（进一步排除 greedy F1=0 的）
79	
80	### 模型在 gold empty 实例上的行为
81	- 598 个 gold empty 实例中，579 个模型也输出空（96.8%）
82	- 仅 19 个产生了假阳性预测
83	
84	**结论：gold empty 处理正确，不是 bug。但 63.8% 训练 empty 率导致模型习得过强的"空输出"先验。**
85	
86	---
87	
88	## 方向 4：Train/Eval Loss vs 推理 F1 差距
89	
90	### 训练日志
91	
92	| Epoch | Train Loss | Eval Loss |
93	|-------|-----------|-----------|
94	| ~1 | 0.2080 | 0.0880 |
95	| ~2 | 0.0470 | 0.0857 |
96	| ~3 | 0.0300 | **0.0772** (最佳) |
97	| ~4 | 0.0240 | 0.0788 |
98	| ~5 | 0.0210 | 0.0896 (回升) |
99	
100	- 模型用最终 checkpoint（epoch 5, step 1065），但 epoch 3 的 eval loss 最低
101	- Eval loss 在 epoch 5 回升 → 轻微过拟合
102	- 训练使用 LoRA（87M trainable / 8.3B total = 1.05%），5 epochs，batch 16
103	
104	### 关键问题
105	- **训练的 eval set = dev set**（1009 实例），与 test set（1287 实例）是不同数据切分
106	- 模型确实是在 WNUT-17 上训练的（非 SciERC zero-shot）
107	- Eval loss 低（0.077-0.089）但推理 F1 仅 0.525 → loss 被大量空实例拉低（空实例 loss 很小，只需输出 `{"entities": [], ...}`）
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Logprob 反向相关解释
112	
113	| 子集 | Mean Logprob | 说明 |
114	|------|-------------|------|
115	| 空预测（n=260） | **-0.007** | 极高置信 |
116	| 非空预测 F1=0（n=95） | -0.054 | 中等置信 |
117	| 非空预测 F1>0（n=334） | -0.046 | 中等置信 |
118	
119	**机制**：模型预测空输出时置信度最高（logprob 接近 0），因为训练数据中 63.8% 是空实例。在 gold 非空的 689 实例中：
120	- 高 logprob → 很可能是空预测 → F1=0 → **负相关 (rho = -0.41)**
121	- 在 conditional 集（F1>0, n=334）中，logprob rho = +0.35 → 模型对非空预测的置信度确实有区分力
122	
123	### SJ 高但 rho 低的原因
124	- 155 个实例：16 个 sample 全部为空 → SJ = 1.0 但 F1 = 0
125	- 这些高一致性 + 零 F1 的点拉平了整体相关性
126	- Conditional 集 SJ rho = 0.288，显著高于 full 集的 0.089
127	
128	---
129	
130	## 根因判断
131	
132	**主因：训练数据空实例过多（63.8%）— 数据构造策略问题，非转换 bug。**
133	
134	| 因素 | 类别 | 影响程度 |
135	|------|------|---------|
136	| 训练集 63.8% 空实例 | 数据策略 | **致命** — 导致 73% 的 F1=0 |
137	| WNUT-17 社交媒体噪声 | 方法边界 | 中等 — 导致 27% 的 F1=0 |
138	| Prompt 模板微小差异 | 次要 bug | 轻微 |
139	| Epoch 5 轻微过拟合 | 训练策略 | 轻微 |
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 修复建议
144	
145	### P0：降低训练空实例比例
146	将空实例从 63.8% 下采样到 ≤25%（保留 ~400 个空实例 + 1228 个有实体 = 空占比 24.6%），重新训练。这是最直接的修复。
147	
148	### P1：使用 best checkpoint
149	训练时加 `save_best_model=True`（按 eval_loss），或手动使用 epoch 3 的 checkpoint（step 600, eval_loss=0.077）而非最终的 epoch 5。
150	
151	### P2：评估指标选择
152	对于 WNUT-17 这类 high-empty-rate 数据集，使用 conditional 指标（排除 F1=0）作为主信号，full 指标仅作参考。当前 conditional SJ rho = 0.288, logprob rho = 0.350 表明方法在非空预测上有效。
153	
154	### P3：金标质量 review
155	WNUT-17 存在标注噪声（如 `Bhangra` = person, `Zlatan` = product），但这是数据集固有问题，非我方可控。
156

175	\paragraph{Capability stratification.}
176	SJ effectiveness scales with structural complexity: on SciERC instances with 6+ entities, $\rho{=}0.547$, compared to $\rho{=}0.415$ for 1--2 entities.
177	Similarly, RE instances with ${\geq}3$ relation triples ($n{=}81$) yield substantially stronger correlations (Voting $\rho{=}0.630$, SJ $\rho{=}0.502$), demonstrating that within the model's capability range, increased output complexity amplifies structural signal advantage.
178	The SJ advantage over logprob remains stable across sentence-length quartiles ($\Delta\rho{\approx}0.08$--$0.20$), and three independent complexity proxies (entity count, sentence length, relation density) show weak mutual correlation ($|r|{<}0.15$), indicating a genuinely multi-dimensional benefit rather than a single confound.
179	
180	\paragraph{Method boundary: WNUT-17.}
181	WNUT-17 establishes where the approach breaks down.
182	SJ achieves $\rho{=}0.062$ ($p{=}0.106$, not statistically significant), with 54\% of instances at zero F1.
183	Log-probability shows a strong \textit{negative} correlation ($\rho{=}{-}0.411$): the model is confidently wrong on novel entities, a calibration failure that no post-hoc consistency signal can remedy.
184	This is a boundary of the method, not a limitation of the datasets.
